bullets: Game 8 of 8 in the video, and a win from behind: he takes the enemy left tower to 2448 of 4858 HP by clock 1:51, loses the initiative to a Cannon Cart / Mortar counter-push (own right tower to 2959, "Yeah, we're dead. Okay, well, this is GG's, I think", t=1400-1402), then wins in overtime on the same tower — "The piggy. The piggy. Let's go. Dude, we won. We just have to cycle back. What a win, man" (t=1481-1485).

The pattern is Rune Giant from his own back line (tiles [8, 0], [8, 0], [10, 0], [8, 0]) with Berserker and Mother Witch walked in front of it, never the tank at the bridge; the bridge pressure comes from Berserker and Elite Barbarians instead.

Mother Witch is the real win condition: he plays her into crowded pushes for the Cursed Hog conversions ("I just want to get as many piggies as possible... maybe two piggies if we're lucky", t=1271-1275), spends Heal Spirit to keep her alive ("Keep the Mother Witch on full HP", t=1293), and it is the Cursed Hogs that finish the game in overtime.

Berserker is the Hero: Savage Survival is popped for survival ("Let's pop the ability just to keep this alive so we can take out that mortar", t=1355), weighed against spending 6 elixir ("I could probably just Berserker push this ability", t=1324), and held for the final tower push ("we got the ability. That's huge", t=1471).

Elite Barbarians are placed by threat, not by habit: at the bridge only with Mother Witch already supporting (t=1278-1281), early on his own half to line up the Rune Giant buff ("I want to do it early so my Rune Giant has the upgrade available quicker", t=1336), and split across lanes against a Champion ("if I do them in the same lane, then he can just get the crazy Goblin Stine value every time", t=1376).

Minions and Heal Spirit are cheap insurance rather than offence — Minions behind the push to "clean up any type of counter push" (t=1345), Heal Spirit onto his own units — while Evo Zap and Fireball do the finishing, including a Fireball on the tower purely for free chip when he thought the game was lost (t=1406-1412), which is what put the overtime win in range.

His stated verdict on the deck, twice: "This deck is just so punishing, man. Any slight mistake and you're just cooked" (t=1305-1308), tempered by "Obviously, if he defends like this every single time, I think he'll be chilling, but... it's going to be very hard to defend like that every time" (t=1348-1353).

new_deck.rationale: The pressure comes from cheap fast units placed at the bridge (Berserker, Elite Barbarians, Mother Witch) rather than from a slow back-line build-up, with the 4-elixir Rune Giant acting as a cheap tank and damage buff rather than a beatdown centrepiece.
new_deck.why_it_works_md: The Rune Giant costs only 4, so she can go down in the back without conceding the tempo a real beatdown tank would, and her enchant turns the deck's fast, low-damage hitters — Berserker above all — into real threats on every third attack. Mother Witch supplies the second win condition: she is played into whatever the opponent commits to the push, and the Cursed Hogs she leaves behind convert a successful defence directly into tower damage, which is exactly how this match was won from behind in overtime. Berserker's Hero ability (Savage Survival, 3 elixir) makes her survivable enough to lead a bridge push or to hold a lane on defence, and Heal Spirit plus Minions keep the counter-push cheap so the Fireball and Evo Zap slots are free for finishing. The weakness Ryley names himself is that a disciplined defender can hold it: "if he defends like this every single time, I think he'll be chilling".
